title: Big numbers and prices
intro: The Mosquito King has moved into your Hà Nội flat and set up a stall, and every price he quotes is a rip-off. Beat him with the numbers you need for real prices, and the words for cheap, expensive and more.

foe.name: Vua Muỗi
foe.intro: Every price he quotes is chặt chém, Vietnamese for a rip-off: literally "chop and slash".

taunts.vi: Vo ve! Một, hai, ba... đốt!

win.vi: Ối! Thôi, trả lại tiền cho bạn đây!
win.en: Ouch! Fine, here is your money back!

lose.vi: Vo ve! Mai tôi lại đến!

words.hook: A hundred chums squeezed onto one bench, all humming one calm, level "chum".
words.tip: In Hà Nội, tr sounds like ch, so trăm sounds like "chum". ă is a short, quick a. Keep the tone level.

words.hook: Say "sing in" and drop the "si": "ngin". A thousand singers, every voice sinking low.
words.tip: ngh is the ng of "sing" (written ngh before i, e and ê). The huyền tone falls gently. The South says ngàn.

words.hook: A million mosquitoes squeal "chee-ew" in one quick beat, and each bite lands with a heavy thud, like the nặng tone.
words.tip: In Hà Nội, tr sounds like ch. iê glides from "ee" to "eh", then u. Nặng drops low and stops short in the throat.

words.hook: The Fat Cat returns with twenty kittens (hai mươi), all crying one calm, level note. Ten on its own, mười, sighs down.
words.tip: Like mười, but level: no fall.
words.note: After mươi, 1 becomes mốt: hai mươi mốt is 21. At stalls people drop nghìn: "Năm mươi!" means 50.000₫, and menus write 50k.

words.en: five, after mười or mươi (mười lăm = 15)
words.hook: A lamb takes the five's place in 15, 25 and 35; say it short, like "lum" (rhymes with "chum"), calm and level. Leave năm there and hai mươi năm means "twenty years".
words.tip: ă is short. Keep it level.

words.en: zero (for an empty tens place, as in 105)
words.hook: Picture 1_5 with an empty slot in the middle, where a tiny bell rings one flat "ling".
words.tip: Hà Nội says một trăm linh năm for 105; the South says lẻ. In Hà Nội, linh sounds close to English "ling". Keep the tone level.

words.note: It follows the unit: hai nghìn rưỡi is 2,500; một tiếng rưỡi is an hour and a half.
words.hook: Your voice cracks halfway through the word, just as the number breaks into a half.
words.tip: In Hà Nội, r sounds like z. ươi glides from ư to ơ to i. The ngã tone breaks in the middle, then jumps up.

words.hook: Slide "tee" into "ten" in one syllable: tiền, a sad falling sigh as your money leaves your wallet.
words.tip: t has no puff of air. iê glides from "ee" to "eh". The huyền tone falls gently.

words.hook: Ding-DONG: the doorbell's second note sinks, like huyền. It is the landlord, and he wants your đồng.
words.tip: đ is a firm d with the tongue behind the top teeth. ô is tighter than the o of English "dong", and in Hà Nội the lips close at the end, so it sounds close to "dohm".

words.hook: "Bow, new." You bow to the seller and, keeping your voice flat, ask how much the new thing costs.
words.tip: nh is like the ny in "canyon". Both syllables stay level.

words.hook: "Dut!" (rhymes with "but") you yelp as the price shoots up, just like the rising tone.
words.tip: ă is short. The final t is cut off, not released. The South says mắc.

words.hook: It is so cheap your voice drops low in disbelief, "zeh...": really, that cheap?
words.tip: In Hà Nội, r sounds like z. e is open, like the e in "bed". Hỏi starts at your normal pitch and drops further and faster than huyền; said alone it may lift a little at the end. The hỏi mark is a question mark without its dot.

words.hook: Say British "her" with an n on the end: hơn, a little more. Round your lips and it becomes hôn, a kiss, which is more than a hug.
words.tip: ơ is the vowel of British "fur" with no r; ô is a tight, rounded o. Keep the tone level.
words.note: It goes after the describing word: rẻ hơn is cheaper, đắt hơn is more expensive.

words.hook: Oliver Twist holds up his bowl for more; his voice cracks, then jumps: "Nữa!"
words.tip: ưa glides from ư ("oo" with spread lips) to a short "uh". The ngã tone breaks, then jumps high.

grammar.title: Big numbers, biggest part first
grammar.text: Numbers go biggest part first, with mươi for the tens from 20 up (10 to 19 use mười): hai trăm năm mươi is 250. After mười or mươi, 5 becomes lăm: hai mươi lăm is 25. An empty tens place is linh: một trăm linh năm is 105.

combos.vi: Phở gà bốn mươi lăm nghìn
combos.note: Spoken fast: bốn lăm nghìn, and many Hà Nội speakers say bốn nhăm.

combos.vi: Bún cá ba mươi lăm nghìn

combos.note: Not 25: after mươi, five is lăm. With năm it means years.
Literally "how much money?". The standard way to ask a price.
quá after a word means "so", as in Ngon quá!
